content.user_title: Coordinate Cursor and Claude Code Workflows
content.value_statement: Teams using two AI agents need clear roles, task states, and handoff rules. This skill explains a Cursor and Claude Code workflow with examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains Cursor and Claude Code role boundaries for PM and worker tasks.
Defines Plans.md status markers for requested, in-progress, completed, reviewed, and blocked tasks.
Describes handoff flow from task request to implementation, report, review, and production decision.
Documents command references for initialization, planning, work execution, status sync, and handoff.
Provides examples for new features, urgent bugs, CI failures, and parallel task handling.
States the three-failure CI escalation rule for Claude Code work.
limitations: It explains workflow concepts; it does not execute commands or modify project files.
It assumes a repository uses Plans.md and compatible handoff commands.
It does not replace project-specific release, security, or deployment policies.
Most source examples are in Japanese, so teams may need localization.

use_cases.title: Onboard A Development Team
use_cases.description: Introduce a shared Cursor and Claude Code delivery process with clear responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Track Solo AI Work
use_cases.description: Use Plans.md status markers to keep AI-assisted work visible and reviewable.

use_cases.title: Review Release Handoffs
use_cases.description: Check how completed work, staging validation, and production approval pass between agents.

prompt_templates.title: Explain The Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Cursor and Claude Code should share work in this two-agent workflow. Focus on roles, handoffs, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Task States
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to track a feature from request to review using Plans.md status markers from this workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a handoff plan for this feature using the workflow guide: [describe feature]. Include owner, status marker, review needs, and escalation criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Workflow Adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our current AI development process against this workflow. Identify missing role boundaries, unclear handoffs, CI escalation gaps, and production approval risks.

output_examples.input: Explain the workflow to a new teammate.
output_examples.output: Cursor acts as PM and assigns tasks. Claude Code implements, tests, and reports back. Cursor reviews staging results before production decisions.

output_examples.input: What happens after three CI failures?
output_examples.output: Claude Code stops automatic fixes, writes an escalation report, lists attempted fixes, and asks Cursor for a decision.

output_examples.input: How should multiple independent tasks run?
output_examples.output: Claude Code may run independent tasks in parallel. Dependent tasks should remain sequential to avoid conflicting changes.

best_practices: Keep Plans.md current before and after each handoff.
Let Claude Code handle implementation and staging checks, then keep production approval with the PM role.
Escalate repeated CI failures after three attempts with a clear report.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation without a visible task state or owner.
Treating staging success as automatic production approval.
Retrying CI fixes indefinitely instead of escalating.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a guide and only documents workflow commands and expected roles.

faq.question: Who should approve production deployment?
faq.answer: The workflow keeps production deployment decisions with Cursor or the PM role.

faq.question: Can one person use this workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. A solo developer can use the same task states to separate planning, implementation, and review.

faq.question: What file does the workflow use for task tracking?
faq.answer: It centers on Plans.md as the shared task list and status source.

faq.question: Does it support Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace report lists Codex compatibility, but the source content focuses on Cursor and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should happen when a task is unclear?
faq.answer: The guide recommends clarifying with Cursor or using the status command to summarize the current state.
